findings.explanation: The template sets no shielded_vm_config block, so enable_secure_boot defaults to false and every runtime created from it boots without verified-boot protection against bootkits/rootkits. The module otherwise hardens the runtime (CMEK, no internet, idle shutdown), so this is the outlier. No deterministic holden policy covers shielded_vm_config on google_colab_runtime_template (HLD_GCP_244/245 cover google_notebooks_instance only).
findings.remediation: Add a shielded_vm_config block with enable_secure_boot driven by a new enable_secure_boot variable defaulting to true.
findings.resolution: Fixed: added shielded_vm_config { enable_secure_boot = var.enable_secure_boot } with new variable enable_secure_boot (bool, default true).
findings.title: Colab runtime template does not enable Shielded VM secure boot

findings.explanation: Vertex AI requires the CMEK key to live in the same region as the resource. var.kms_key_name accepts any non-empty string, so a key ring in another location (or a key name instead of a full resource ID) passes plan and only fails when the API rejects the create. Principle is a best fit: this is apply-time correctness rather than a security gap, since CMEK is already mandatory.
findings.remediation: Validate the full projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/* format in variables.tf and add a precondition on the runtime template that the key's location matches var.location.
findings.resolution: Fixed: var.kms_key_name now validated against the full projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/* format, and a lifecycle precondition on the runtime template requires the key's location to equal var.location.
findings.title: kms_key_name is only checked for non-empty; a malformed key or a key in another region fails late at apply

findings.explanation: The route is named restricted_apis / colab-restricted-googleapis and its comment says it routes the restricted VIP range, but 199.36.153.8/30 is private.googleapis.com (restricted.googleapis.com is 199.36.153.4/30), and the DNS records resolve to private.googleapis.com. A reader copying this example would believe they had the VPC-SC-only restricted VIP when they have the general private VIP. The config is internally consistent; the naming and comment are wrong.
findings.remediation: Rename the route to private_apis / colab-private-googleapis and correct the comments to describe the private VIP (or switch both route and DNS to the restricted VIP if VPC-SC is intended).
findings.resolution: Fixed: route renamed to google_compute_route.private_apis (colab-private-googleapis), comments corrected to the private.googleapis.com VIP with a note on switching to restricted.googleapis.com under VPC-SC.
findings.title: Example route and comments say 'restricted' VIP but configure the private.googleapis.com VIP

suggested_policies.rationale: Secure boot is off by default on google_colab_runtime_template, so runtimes boot without verified-boot protection. HLD_GCP_244/245 enforce Shielded VM on Vertex AI Notebooks but nothing covers Colab Enterprise templates.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: Colab Enterprise runtime templates must enable Shielded VM secure boot
principle: supply-chain
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Secure boot is off by default on google_colab_runtime_template, so runtimes boot without verified-boot protection. HLD_GCP_244/245 enforce Shielded VM on Vertex AI Notebooks but nothing covers Colab Enterprise templates.
message: |
  google_colab_runtime_template does not set shielded_vm_config.enable_secure_boot = true.
remediation: |
  ```hcl
  resource "google_colab_runtime_template" "main" {
    shielded_vm_config {
      enable_secure_boot = true
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_colab_runtime_template:
    path: shielded_vm_config.enable_secure_boot
    equals: true

suggested_policies.rationale: network_spec.enable_internet_access = true gives every notebook runtime a direct public internet path, an exfiltration and download channel for arbitrary code. HLD_GCP_235 enforces the equivalent on Vertex AI Notebooks runtimes but nothing covers google_colab_runtime_template.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_002
name: Colab Enterprise runtime templates must disable internet access
principle: network-security
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  network_spec.enable_internet_access = true gives every notebook runtime a direct public internet path, an exfiltration and download channel for arbitrary code. HLD_GCP_235 enforces the equivalent on Vertex AI Notebooks runtimes but nothing covers google_colab_runtime_template.
message: |
  google_colab_runtime_template does not set network_spec.enable_internet_access = false.
remediation: |
  ```hcl
  resource "google_colab_runtime_template" "main" {
    network_spec {
      enable_internet_access = false
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_colab_runtime_template:
    path: network_spec.enable_internet_access
    equals: false
